subproblem.title: Upper density theorem: a measure finite on compact sets has zero n-density on a Borel set at H^n-almost every point outside it
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and let A ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set. Then for μHE[n]-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P with x ∉ A, μ(A ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Here B_ρ(x) is the open ball, ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n, ρ^n is entered via ENNReal.ofReal, and the quotient is computed in [0, ∞]. (In the parent's notation: D(μ⌞A, x) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ A; no restriction on n.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet A → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), x ∉ A → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => μ (A ∩ ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 (Upper Density Theorem) together with Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 698–721). Its printed proof uses the comparison Theorem 3.3 and the 5-times covering Lemma 3.4 (lines 602–697): for t > 0 and closed C ⊆ A, every point of S_t := {x ∉ A : D(μ⌞A, x) ≥ t} satisfies D(μ⌞(A ∖ C), x) ≥ t, so 3.3 gives t·H^n(S_t) ≤ μ(A ∖ C), which can be made arbitrarily small (Ch. 1, 1.15(2)); Remark 3.7(2) removes μ(A) < ∞ with a cover by open sets of finite measure. Only null sets matter here. So Simon's sharp comparison (normalized H^n, 5-fold enlargement) is replaced below by the crude form t·μH[n](E) ≤ 6^n·μ(G), with Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure μH[n] and a 3-fold Vitali enlargement. The SimonGMT theorem ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside_of_openSigmaFinite (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean), cited in the parent's step 2, formalizes 3.3, 3.6 and 3.7(2) for Borel-regular outer measures. It uses closed-ball quotients and is a.e. for simonHausdorffMeasureReal n, a positive multiple of μH[n]. It is an alternative route, not used here. It would need several conversions: viewing μ as a Borel-regular, open-σ-finite outer measure; Carathéodory measurability of A; transfer of null sets from simonHausdorffMeasureReal n to μHE[n]; and the closed-to-open-ball and ω_n conversions of step 5. The self-contained route below is the one verified in Lean (appendix). Its steps 1–3 adapt the accepted Lean proof of Submission.regcomp_atl_upper_density_zero (candidate commit 031b5125695febe04a82aacb729a15164ef02960), which treats the case μ = H^n⌞S, to an arbitrary measure finite on compact sets.

Notation: H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. By Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, H^n = c_n·μH[n] with c_n = addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ [0, ∞), so every μH[n]-null set is H^n-null. ω := unitBallVolume n = vol(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝ^n). B_ρ(x) is the open ball and B̄_ρ(x) the closed ball. For S ⊆ ℝ^P and x ∈ ℝ^P put q_x^S(ρ) := μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)^n ∈ [0, ∞]. "ρ ↓ 0" means the filter 𝓝[>] 0.

1. (Vitali selection, Simon 3.4.) Let E ⊆ ℝ^P, δ > 0, and let p(y, r) be a property of pairs such that every x ∈ E has some ρ ∈ (0, δ) with p(x, ρ). Claim: there is a countable set u of pairs (y, r) with the following properties:
- y ∈ E, r ∈ (0, δ) and p(y, r) for each (y, r) ∈ u;
- the closed balls B̄_r(y), (y, r) ∈ u, are pairwise disjoint;
- E ⊆ ⋃_{(y,r)∈u} B̄_{3r}(y).
Proof. Apply Mathlib's Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement to the closed balls B̄_r(y), (y, r) ∈ F := {(y, r) : y ∈ E, 0 < r < δ, p(y, r)}, with radius function (y, r) ↦ r (bounded by δ), factor τ = 2, and nonempty balls. It yields a pairwise disjoint subfamily u ⊆ F such that every (x, ρ) ∈ F has some (y, r) ∈ u with B̄_ρ(x) ∩ B̄_r(y) ≠ ∅ and ρ ≤ 2r. Pick w in that intersection. Then |x − y| ≤ |x − w| + |w − y| ≤ ρ + r ≤ 3r, so x ∈ B̄_{3r}(y). Every x ∈ E lies in some (x, ρ) ∈ F, so E ⊆ ⋃_u B̄_{3r}(y). The selected balls are pairwise disjoint and have nonempty interior (they contain B_r(y), r > 0). Hence u is countable, since ℝ^P is separable (Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior).

2. (Comparison, Simon 3.3 with constant 6^n.) Let t ∈ (0, ∞), E ⊆ ℝ^P, and let G ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Suppose that for every x ∈ E and every δ > 0 there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with t·ofReal(ρ)^n ≤ μ(G ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). Claim: t·μH[n](E) ≤ 6^n·μ(G).
Proof. For j ∈ ℕ, apply step 1 with δ_j := 1/(j + 1) and p(y, r) :⟺ t·ofReal(r)^n ≤ μ(G ∩ B̄_r(y)). This gives countable families u_j.
(a) Packing. The sets G ∩ B̄_r(y), (y, r) ∈ u_j, are pairwise disjoint Borel subsets of G. By countable additivity (measure_biUnion),
 t·Σ_{u_j} ofReal(r)^n ≤ Σ_{u_j} μ(G ∩ B̄_r(y)) = μ(⋃_{u_j} G ∩ B̄_r(y)) ≤ μ(G).
(b) Covering. E ⊆ ⋃_{u_j} B̄_{3r}(y), and diam B̄_{3r}(y) ≤ 6r ≤ ofReal(6/(j + 1)) → 0 as j → ∞. Also (diam B̄_{3r}(y))^n ≤ ofReal(6r)^n = 6^n·ofReal(r)^n. The definition of Hausdorff measure (Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum) and (a) give
 μH[n](E) ≤ liminf_j Σ_{u_j} (diam B̄_{3r}(y))^n ≤ 6^n·μ(G)/t.
The last step bounds every term of the sequence (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le, t ≠ 0, ∞). Multiplying by t (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel) gives the claim. For n = 0 all n-th powers equal 1 and the argument is unchanged.

3. (Finite case, Simon 3.6.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with μ(S) < ∞. Claim: for H^n-a.e. x ∉ S, q_x^S(ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
(a) Fix t ∈ (0, ∞) and let N_t := {x ∉ S : t < q_x^S(ρ) for arbitrarily small ρ > 0}, i.e. ∃ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] 0. We show μH[n](N_t) = 0. Let ε > 0.
- The measure μ⌞S is finite, hence weakly regular on the metric space ℝ^P (Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure).
- So there is a closed F ⊆ S with μ(S ∖ F) < t·ε/6^n (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt). Put G := S ∖ F; it is Borel.
- Let x ∈ N_t and δ > 0. As x ∉ S ⊇ F and F is closed, there is r₁ > 0 with B_{r₁}(x) ∩ F = ∅.
- Choose ρ ∈ (0, min(δ, r₁/2)) with t < q_x^S(ρ). This means t·ofReal(ρ)^n < μ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt, as ofReal(ρ)^n ∈ (0, ∞)).
- Since B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ B_{r₁}(x) misses F, S ∩ B̄_ρ(x) = G ∩ B̄_ρ(x).
Thus the hypothesis of step 2 holds for E := N_t and this G, so
 t·μH[n](N_t) ≤ 6^n·μ(G) < 6^n·t·ε/6^n = t·ε,
and μH[n](N_t) < ε (cancel t ∈ (0, ∞)). As ε > 0 was arbitrary, μH[n](N_t) = 0, hence H^n(N_t) = c_n·0 = 0.
(b) Let x ∉ S with q_x^S(ρ) not tending to 0. Then there is ε > 0 with q_x^S(ρ) > ε for arbitrarily small ρ > 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero). Choose k ∈ ℕ with 1/k < ε (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt). Since 1/(k + 1) ≤ 1/k, x ∈ N_{1/(k+1)}. So the exceptional set lies in ⋃_{k∈ℕ} N_{1/(k+1)}, which is H^n-null by (a) and countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null).

4. (Localization; a variant of Simon 3.7(2) with V_j := B_j(0), localizing the set A to A ∩ V_j instead of the measure μ to μ⌞V_j.) For j ∈ ℕ let A_j := A ∩ B_j(0). It is Borel, and μ(A_j) ≤ μ(B̄_j(0)) < ∞ because closed balls of ℝ^P are compact. By step 3 and countability (ae_all_iff), for H^n-a.e. x the following holds: for every j with x ∉ A_j, q_x^{A_j}(ρ) → 0. Fix such an x with x ∉ A, and choose j ∈ ℕ with j > |x| + 1. Then x ∉ A_j, so q_x^{A_j}(ρ) → 0. For 0 < ρ < 1 and y ∈ A ∩ B_ρ(x) we have |y| ≤ |x| + |y − x| < |x| + 1 < j. Hence A ∩ B_ρ(x) ⊆ A_j ∩ B̄_ρ(x).

5. (Normalization and conclusion.) ω ∈ (0, ∞): B_1(0) ⊆ ℝ^n is a nonempty open set and volume is an additive Haar measure (measure_ball_pos), and the ball is bounded (measure_ball_lt_top). For 0 < ρ < 1 we have ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(ρ)^n (ENNReal.ofReal_pow). By step 4 and monotonicity of μ,
 0 ≤ μ(A ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω·ofReal(ρ^n)) = ω^{-1}·(μ(A ∩ B_ρ(x))/ofReal(ρ)^n) ≤ ω^{-1}·q_x^{A_j}(ρ).
The equality uses ENNReal.div_eq_inv_mul and ENNReal.mul_inv with ω ≠ 0, ∞. The right side tends to ω^{-1}·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, since ω^{-1} ≠ ∞). By the squeeze theorem, μ(A ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω·ofReal(ρ^n)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. This holds for H^n-a.e. x with x ∉ A, which is the claim. ∎

Localization (Simon 1.3.7(2)): apply the finite case to A_j = A ∩ B_j(0), which agrees with A near x when j > |x| + 1.

subproblem.title: The density of θH^n⌞M equals θ at H^n-almost every point of the carrier
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n (carrier M = R.carrier, multiplicity θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ). The properties of R used are: M is Borel (field measurableSet_carrier); θ is measurable (field measurable_mult) with θ ≥ 1 on M (field mult_pos); and for μHE[n]⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q (field orients). Suppose that μ_R := R.measure = θ·μHE[n]⌞M satisfies μ_R(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Then for μHE[n]-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P with x ∈ M, μ_R(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0. Here B_ρ(x) is the open ball, ω_n = unitBallVolume n, and ρ^n is entered via ENNReal.ofReal. (No restriction on n.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → R.measure K ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), x ∈ R.carrier → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => R.measure (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4–7 of the parent proof. These are Simon Ch. 3, Remarks 1.8(1)–(2) and Theorem 1.9 (chapter-03.txt lines 298–325), with the Upper Density Theorem of Ch. 1, 3.6 and 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 698–721).

The parent's argument is specialized in two ways:
- θ is ℕ-valued. So the Lusin sets M_j of parent step 4 (compact, with θ|M_j continuous) are replaced by the level sets M_k := M ∩ θ^{-1}(k), k ∈ ℕ. These are Borel, θ ≡ k on M_k is trivially continuous, and they cover M exactly, so Lusin's theorem is not needed. Parent steps 5–7 then apply with M_j := M_k; in step 7 the ε of continuity is 0.
- ν := H^n⌞M ≤ μ_R (step 1 below). So the vanishing of D(μ_R⌞(M ∖ M_k), x) implies that of D(ν⌞(M ∖ M_k), x), and the upper density theorem is applied once for each k, with λ = μ_R.
The parent's hypothesis n ≥ 1 is not needed.

Siblings used:
- upper_density_zero (Submission.idtp_dema_upper_density_zero). For every measure λ on ℝ^P that is finite on compact sets and every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P: for H^n-a.e. x with x ∉ A, λ(A ∩ B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → 0.
- tangent_density_one (Submission.rsd_tendsto_closedBall_density_of_approxTangent). If s > 0, H^n(M ∩ B̄_s(x)) ≠ ∞ and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, then H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → 1.
- closed_to_open_ball_density (Submission.rsd_tendsto_ball_density_of_closedBall). For every measure ν', point x and θ' ∈ [0, ∞]: if ν'(B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ', then ν'(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ'.

Notation.
- H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^P.
- M := R.carrier, Borel by the field measurableSet_carrier.
- θ := R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ, measurable by the field measurable_mult.
- ν := H^n⌞M and μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ.
- c(ρ) := ω·ofReal(ρ^n) with ω := unitBallVolume n.
- B_ρ(x) is the open ball and B̄_ρ(x) the closed ball.
- All limits are taken as ρ ↓ 0 (filter 𝓝[>] 0) in [0, ∞].
For every Borel S: μ(S) = ∫_{S∩M} θ dH^n (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), and ν(S) = H^n(S ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_apply).

1. (Local finiteness, parent step 1.) For every Borel S, ν(S) ≤ μ(S). Indeed θ(y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ M (field mult_pos, θ ℕ-valued), so
 ν(S) = ∫_{S∩M} 1 dH^n ≤ ∫_{S∩M} θ dH^n = μ(S) (setLIntegral_mono').
In particular, for every x, H^n(M ∩ B̄_1(x)) = ν(B̄_1(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_1(x)) < ∞, since B̄_1(x) is compact.

2. (Level sets; parent step 4 specialized.) For k ∈ ℕ let A_k := M ∩ θ^{-1}(ℕ ∖ {k}) = M ∖ M_k. It is Borel, since M is Borel and θ is measurable.

3. (Upper densities; parent steps 2 and 4.) Apply upper_density_zero with λ := μ, which is finite on compact sets by hypothesis, and the Borel set A_k. For each k this gives: for H^n-a.e. x, if x ∉ A_k then e_k(ρ) := μ(A_k ∩ B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → 0. As there are countably many k (ae_all_iff), for H^n-a.e. x this holds simultaneously for all k with x ∉ A_k.

4. (Density of ν; parent steps 5–6.) The field orients of R says: for ν-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q (and IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, which is not needed). Since M is Borel, this means: for H^n-a.e. x, if x ∈ M then such a Q exists (ae_restrict_iff'). Fix such x ∈ M and Q.
- By step 1, H^n(M ∩ B̄_1(x)) ≠ ∞. So tangent_density_one with s = 1 gives H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → 1.
- Since ν(B̄_ρ(x)) = H^n(B̄_ρ(x) ∩ M) = H^n(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)), this says ν(B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → 1.
- closed_to_open_ball_density, applied to the measure ν with θ' = 1, gives b(ρ) := ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → 1.

5. (Splitting the ball; parent step 7.) Let x ∈ M be a point at which steps 3 and 4 hold; this is the case for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M. Let k := θ(x) and T := θ^{-1}(k), a Borel set. Then x ∉ A_k, so e_k(ρ) → 0 by step 3. Fix ρ and write B := B_ρ(x). The set B ∩ M is the disjoint union of (B ∩ M) ∩ T and (B ∩ M) ∖ T = (A_k ∩ B) ∩ M, and θ ≡ k on T. Hence (lintegral_inter_add_sdiff, setLIntegral_congr_fun, lintegral_const)
 μ(B) = ∫_{(B∩M)∩T} θ dH^n + ∫_{(B∩M)∖T} θ dH^n = k·H^n((B ∩ M) ∩ T) + μ(A_k ∩ B).
Similarly (measure_inter_add_sdiff)
 ν(B) = H^n((B ∩ M) ∩ T) + ν(A_k ∩ B).
Now use H^n((B ∩ M) ∩ T) ≤ H^n(B ∩ M) = ν(B), and ν(A_k ∩ B) ≤ μ(A_k ∩ B) (step 1). This gives
 (U) μ(B) ≤ k·ν(B) + μ(A_k ∩ B);
 (L) k·ν(B) ≤ μ(B) + k·μ(A_k ∩ B).

6. (Limits.) Let a(ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ). Divide (U) and (L) by c(ρ) (ENNReal.div_le_div_right, ENNReal.add_div, mul_div_assoc). This gives
 k·b(ρ) − k·e_k(ρ) ≤ a(ρ) ≤ k·b(ρ) + e_k(ρ),
where the left inequality is (L) rewritten with truncated subtraction (tsub_le_iff_right). Since k ∈ ℕ is finite, b(ρ) → 1 and e_k(ρ) → 0:
- k·b(ρ) + e_k(ρ) → k·1 + 0 = k (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, Tendsto.add);
- k·b(ρ) − k·e_k(ρ) → k − 0 = k (ENNReal.Tendsto.sub, the limit k being finite).
By the squeeze theorem, a(ρ) → k = θ(x).

7. (Conclusion.) The set of x ∈ M at which the conclusion fails lies in the union of the H^n-null exceptional sets of steps 3 and 4. Hence for H^n-a.e. x with x ∈ M, μ(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ(x). ∎
